name: Standing Escape
description: Standing after Invisible Collar requires releasing the high guard, creating space and establishing safe posts. The facing leg clinch contains no rear hooks.
summary: Standing after a high-guard reset requires releasing Invisible Collar, creating space and establishing a stable base before rising.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. A technical stand-up needs disengaged space and supporting posts. It is not a direct escape from rear hooks inside the facing leg clinch.

The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What must open before you prepare to rise?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player must release the facing Invisible Collar enclosure before creating space and posts for standing.

plausible: Only second leg; first holds neck
Only hand grip; high leg curled
trap: Only overhook; legs still hold head

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): Which loading must end before the leg comes down?
flashcards.answer: Unload captured neck and shoulder connections before lowering the high legs into the guard reset.

plausible: Only free-foot pressure on the mat
Only the opponent's mat post
trap: Only leg cross; arm wrap still pulls

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): How does the high knee return toward ordinary guard?
flashcards.answer: Create a free path with the hips rather than dragging the foot against the knee while the upper body remains entangled.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower leg through a free hip angle

plausible: Pull foot down with knee fixed high
Straighten leg into their shoulder
trap: Keep ankle grip; flatten hip first

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What should you keep between you while creating distance?
flashcards.answer: Guard retention comes first: keep forearm and knee between the bodies until the opponent's chest pressure no longer reaches you.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside forearm and knee barrier

plausible: Hands on floor, torso gap left open
Legs outside, hands reach for head

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): Which orientation helps you preserve that distance?
flashcards.answer: Keep shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent while the framed hip escape creates room.
flashcards.answer_line: Face them while your hips move

plausible: Turn back before the knee returns
Chest down beneath their pressure

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): When can supporting posts be established?
flashcards.answer: Create distance after releasing the clinch, then establish stable hand and foot posts for standing.
flashcards.answer_line: Once frames free your chest space

plausible: While their chest still pins yours
While both high legs hold their head
trap: Once ankles open, before knee space

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): Why retain an inside knee before making your supporting posts?
flashcards.answer: An inside knee and forearm preserve distance after the high clinch opens. Establish posts only when the opponent cannot pin your torso with chest pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep chest away to make rising space

plausible: Keep high loop closed while standing
Replace the supporting hand post

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What does a stand-up need beyond opening the high legs?
flashcards.answer: Releasing the high guard is only the first phase. Rising needs enough distance and a supported base.
flashcards.answer_line: Space with firm hand and foot posts

plausible: Only free hand, chest pressure stays
Only the opponent's head rising
trap: Hand post with both feet caught

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): The neck loop remains loaded as you sit up; what now?
flashcards.answer: Stop the rise and open the leg-and-arm enclosure rather than lifting or rotating a neck still caught inside it.

plausible: Sit up until the loop pulls apart
Keep loop, move both feet under you
trap: Post hand behind, leg curl tight

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (bottom): What confirms readiness for the separate standing phase?
flashcards.answer: After guard recovery creates distance, confirm a stable hand-and-foot base before initiating the separately taught stand-up.
flashcards.answer_line: Space, firm hand and foot posts

plausible: High leg open, chest still pins you
Hands free, both feet still caught
trap: Hands off mat, chest pressure stays

defender.description: Standing Escape (defender): The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. A technical stand-up needs disengaged space and supporting posts. It is not a direct escape from rear hooks inside the facing leg clinch.

The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure. Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.

Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm. Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens. Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

A high Invisible Collar enclosure can still apply vascular choke pressure during a posture change. Signal early and wait for the arm-and-leg connection to open completely; the other player beginning to stand does not make a trapped neck safe to lift.

Keep a balanced base: Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.
Address the leg enclosure: Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm.
Recover inside position: Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens.
Stop on compression: Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What can still enclose your head as they sit up?
flashcards.answer: A bottom player changing posture does not prove their Invisible Collar has opened; check the remaining head and shoulder connection.
flashcards.answer_line: High leg-and-arm loop round the head

plausible: Low knee frame after high legs drop
Loose ankle, thighs off shoulders

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): How should you remain aligned during their reset?
flashcards.answer: Avoid turning the head or torso away while the arm remains caught; wait for usable slack in the upper-body enclosure.

plausible: Head turns away, elbow held outside
Shoulder turns back, wrist pinned

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): If the high loop is applying choke pressure, what first?
flashcards.answer: A loaded neck enclosure needs immediate release, even if the bottom player has started a posture change toward standing.
flashcards.answer_line: Tap; get the high loop released

plausible: Wait until they stand before tapping
Lift chest to drag your neck free
trap: Tap while lifting head through loop

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): What should create room before you lift your head?
flashcards.answer: Use early balanced positioning to open the high connection before head extraction; do not force an already loaded neck.
flashcards.answer_line: Slack at high leg's hip and thigh

plausible: Only widen your stance on the floor
Only their hand posts on the mat
trap: Only free leg down; high thigh tight

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar stand-up (top): Where should the freed arm return as they disengage?
flashcards.answer: Recover a compact inside elbow after the high closure opens so the arm is not left outside for renewed isolation.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside by ribs, available to frame

plausible: Wide on the mat beyond their hips
Across far shoulder, elbow flared
trap: Hand in, elbow outside their thigh
